methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target equitable skill-building at the community level, signaling distributed deep learning through peer networks rather than platform dependency—a classic Build It Yourself indicator if sustained beyond individual initiatives.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's pediatric AI collaboration with Children's National concentrates advanced research capability in established academic hubs, reinforcing specialized excellence in metro-adjacent institutions rather than distributing AI R&D capacity across underserved regions.

signals.title: Data center supply chains are moving into rural areas that need jobs. This complicates the debate over taxation.
signals.signal_reading: While data center supply chains bring manufacturing jobs to rural areas, this creates economic dependency on infrastructure that serves concentrated AI compute elsewhere—rural regions provide power and parts but not AI capability development, deepening functional inequality.

signals.title: New artificial intelligence minor launches this fall - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's new AI minor formalizes deep technical education but concentrates that knowledge-building in an established research university, creating credential pathways for those already proximate to higher ed rather than distributed fluency mechanisms.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard's AI help assistant (Amelia) represents platform-delivered automation for workforce support—users interact with AI tools without building underlying capability, signaling shallow but functional adoption in defense-industrial contexts.
